answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I cannot tell what is causing the knee pain from a written description, and I would rather not put a name to it. Sharp pain on downhills, aching on stairs, and pain that grew over the week are all reasons to have a physio or sports doctor examine the right knee this week.

No, skip the tempo for now. Next week's Wednesday is an easy run instead, and the hard session stays off until a physio has looked at the knee and you have had several pain-free easy runs in a row.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed

Four of this week's five runs matched the plan in distance, and the Wednesday tempo was close to its target. The middle block ran near 8:00 per mile, and the easy days held at 138 to 139 bpm, so the aerobic work landed where it should.

The Sunday long run did not match. The plan asked for 13 miles easy under 150 bpm, and you ran 9.0 miles, stopping at 8.5 and walking the last half mile. That is four miles short of the key session of the week, and it was cut short by pain, not by fatigue.

## The knee

The knee did not start on Sunday. It was tight on the last hill on Thursday, tight before Saturday's run, then sharp on downhills from mile 7 on Sunday. By Monday it hurt on stairs, which you say you have never had before.

Pain that grows across several days is the signal I weight most, more than the volume. I cannot name the cause from a written description, so the right next step is an exam rather than a guess.

## Why next week is smaller

Next week drops the Wednesday tempo and shortens the long run from 13 planned to 8 miles, which is under the 9 miles that ended in pain. Total running falls to about 19 miles, with two non-impact sessions added. A few lighter weeks now protect the build better than pushing a sore knee through long runs, because a running injury this close to race day would cost more time than a short pause.

## What comes after

Once a physio has looked at the knee and you have a run of pain-free easy runs, the long run returns in steps toward 10 miles, and threshold work comes back at a shorter block. The goal has not changed: the long runs still need to build toward 2.5 to 3 hours. Your easy share was 76 percent this week, just under the 80 percent target, so keep easy days truly easy as the load returns.
